papers.title: SP-VLA: A Joint Model Scheduling and Token Pruning Approach for VLA Model Acceleration
papers.title_zh: SP-VLA: A Joint Model Scheduling and Token Pruning Approach for VLA Model Acceleration
papers.abstract_zh: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have attracted increasing attention for their strong control capabilities. However, their high computational cost and low execution frequency hinder their suitability for real-time tasks such as robotic manipulation and autonomous navigation. Existing VLA acceleration methods primarily focus on structural optimization, overlooking the fact that these models operate in sequential decision-making environments. As a result, temporal redundancy in sequential action generation and spatial redundancy in visual input remain unaddressed. To this end, we propose SP-VLA, a unified framework that accelerates VLA models by jointly scheduling models and pruning tokens. Specifically, we design an action-aware model scheduling mechanism that reduces temporal redundancy by dynamically switching between VLA model and a lightweight generator. Inspired by the human motion pattern of focusing on key decision points while relying on intuition for other actions, we categorize VLA actions into deliberative and intuitive, assigning the former to the VLA model and the latter to the lightweight generator, enabling frequency-adaptive execution through collaborative model scheduling. To address spatial redundancy, we further develop a spatio-semantic dual-aware token pruning method. Tokens are classified into spatial and semantic types and pruned based on their dual-aware importance to accelerate VLA inference. These two mechanisms work jointly to guide the VLA in focusing on critical actions and salient visual information, achieving effective acceleration while maintaining high accuracy. Extensive experiments show that our method achieves 1.5$×$ lossless acceleration in LIBERO and 2.4$×$ in SimplerEnv, with up to 6% average performance gain. Inference frequency and latency improve by 2.2$×$ in SimplerEnv and 1.4$×$ in LIBERO.

papers.title: Physics-informed Neural Motion Planning via Domain Decomposition in Large Environments
papers.title_zh: 基于物理信息的神经运动规划：大环境下的域分解方法
papers.tldr_zh: 提出FB-NTFields，通过潜在空间域分解实现大规模运动规划的高效代价估计。
papers.cover_zh: 机器人导航新突破｜不用逐点约束，潜在空间域分解让规划更高效
papers.abstract_zh: 物理信息神经运动规划器（PiN-MPs）提供了一种数据高效的框架，用于求解Eikonal偏微分方程（PDE）并表示运动规划中的代价函数。然而，其可扩展性受到谱偏差和PDE驱动训练的复杂损失景观的限制。域分解通过将环境划分为更小的子域来缓解这些问题，但现有方法仅在单个空间点处强制连续性。虽然这对函数逼近有效，但这些方法无法捕捉运动规划所需的空间连通性，因为代价函数依赖于起点和终点坐标，而非单个查询点。我们提出有限基神经时间场（FB-NTFields），一种用于可扩展代价估计的新型神经场表示。FB-NTFields不在输出空间强制连续性，而是构建潜在空间表示，将代价计算为起点和终点潜在嵌入之间的距离。这实现了全局空间一致性，同时整合了域分解，确保了高效的大规模运动规划。我们在复杂的合成和真实场景中验证了FB-NTFields，展示了相比现有PiN-MPs的显著改进。最后，我们将方法部署在Unitree B1四足机器人上，成功实现了室内环境导航。补充视频见https://youtu.be/OpRuCbLNOwM。
